subject: Human Evolution
title: The Nuchal Ligament
description: A quick, practical guide to The Nuchal Ligament.

hook.text: A ligament runs from the back of your skull down your neck. It does nothing when you walk. Only when you run.

buildup.text: During running, your head pitches forward with each stride. The nuchal ligament snaps it back.

discovery.text: Dogs and horses have it too—animals that run. Chimps and pigs, who don't run far, lack it.

twist.text: Its presence in Homo erectus fossils is evidence that endurance running was part of their survival kit.

climax.text: A tiny ligament in your neck is a 2-million-year-old receipt for an evolutionary investment in running.

punchline.text: A ligament you can't feel proves you were born to run.

quiz.question: What does the nuchal ligament do during running?
options: Stabilizes the head against forward pitching
